children.label: c
children.prompt: Write down $P(X\le2)$. What property of the curve allows this without integration?

answer.worked: The PDF is symmetric about $x=2$, so half its total area lies to the left of $2$. Thus $P(X\le2)=\dfrac12$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Evaluate $P(X\le1)$ and $P(X>1)$. Explain why they add to $1$.

answer.short: $P(X\le1)=\dfrac5{32}$ and $P(X>1)=\dfrac{27}{32}$. These complementary events cover all possible values of $X$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}P(X\le1)&=\frac{3}{32}\left[2x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1\\&=\frac{3}{32}\left(2-\frac13\right)\\&=\frac5{32}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}P(X>1)&=1-\frac5{32}\\&=\frac{27}{32}.\end{aligned}$$
The events are complementary, so their probabilities add to the total probability, $1$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Evaluate $P(X\le0.5)$ and $P(X\ge3.5)$. What do you notice?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}P(X\le0.5)&=\frac{3}{32}\left[2x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{1/2}\\&=\frac{3}{32}\left(\frac12-\frac1{24}\right)\\&=\frac{3}{32}\cdot\frac{11}{24}\\&=\frac{11}{256}.\end{aligned}$$
By symmetry about $x=2$, $P(X\ge3.5)=\dfrac{11}{256}$. The probabilities are equal.

For $0\le x\le4$,
$$\begin{aligned}F(x)&=\int_0^x\frac{3}{32}t(4-t)\,dt\\&=\frac{3}{32}\left[2t^2-\frac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^x\\&=\frac{x^2(6-x)}{32}.\end{aligned}$$
There is no probability below $0$, and all probability lies at or below $4$. Hence
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<0,\\\dfrac{x^2(6-x)}{32},&0\le x\le4,\\1,&x>4.\end{cases}$$

answer.short: $F(x)=0$ for $x<0$; an increasing curve from $(0,0)$ through $(2,\tfrac12)$ to $(4,1)$; $F(x)=1$ for $x>4$.

children.label: j
children.prompt: Find $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ by solving $F(x)=0.25$ and $F(x)=0.75$. Give answers to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{Q_1^2(6-Q_1)}{32}&=\frac14\\Q_1^2(6-Q_1)&=8.\end{aligned}$$
Solving numerically on $[0,4]$ gives $Q_1\approx1.3054$, so $Q_1\approx1.3$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{Q_3^2(6-Q_3)}{32}&=\frac34\\Q_3^2(6-Q_3)&=24.\end{aligned}$$
Solving numerically on $[0,4]$ gives $Q_3\approx2.6946$, so $Q_3\approx2.7$.
